title: Clitoral Complex Anatomy: Glans, Crura & Erectile Bulbs
description: Discover complete clitoral complex anatomy, revealing how the visible glans connects to the internal body, paired crura, vestibular bulbs, and nerve paths.
h1: Clitoral Erectile Complex Anatomy: Glans, Body, Crura and Bulbs
blurb: Beyond the visible glans: the internal clitoral body, paired diverging crura anchored to the ischiopubic rami, vestibular bulbs, and dorsal sensory nerves.
lead: Only the small glans of the clitoris is visible externally; the majority of the clitoral complex arches internally beneath the pubic bones as paired crura and vestibular bulbs. In this illustrated guide to clitoral complex anatomy, we examine 20 documented structures—including clitoral glans, clitoral prepuce, clitoral body, right corpus cavernosum—linking regional topography, tissue architecture, physiological mechanisms, and clinical reasoning.
overview: Only the small glans of the clitoris is visible externally; the majority of the clitoral complex arches internally beneath the pubic bones as paired crura and vestibular bulbs. The visible glans is not the whole clitoris. Two corpora cavernosa join into a body, while proximal crura anchor to the ischiopubic rami. The glans is particularly sensory and is not simply another corpus cavernosum. Paired vestibular bulbs are neighboring erectile tissue flanking the vestibule, anatomically distinguished from the corpora. Arterial inflow, smooth-muscle relaxation and venous outflow restriction contribute to engorgement; somatic sensation travels largely in the dorsal clitoral nerve. Within the human body, the clitoral erectile complex (Clitoris · corpora cavernosa et bulbi vestibuli) is situated in anterior perineum; deep to vulvar surface and along ischiopubic rami, receives arterial perfusion via internal pudendal → deep and dorsal clitoral arteries; posterior labial branches, and is innervated by dorsal nerve of clitoris (pudendal S2–S4); cavernous autonomic fibers via pelvic plexus.

Structurally, the clitoral glans (Glans clitoridis) comprises external distal part beneath or exposed by the hood; dense sensory innervation and distinct histology from cavernous bodies. Physiologically, the clitoral glans governs conveys fine sensation. Structurally, the clitoral prepuce (Preputium clitoridis) comprises fold of skin derived from the anterior labia minora covering part of the glans. Physiologically, the clitoral prepuce protects and permits mobility of glans. Structurally, the clitoral body (Corpus clitoridis) comprises midline body formed by apposition of the paired corpora cavernosa, deep to the external glans. Physiologically, the clitoral body governs engorges via cavernous vascular spaces. The right corpus cavernosum (Corpus cavernosum dextrum) is one of the paired erectile cylinders of the clitoral body, enclosed by tunica albuginea. Physiologically, the right corpus cavernosum governs fills with blood during arousal. Structurally, the left corpus cavernosum (Corpus cavernosum sinistrum) comprises contralateral cavernous cylinder joining the body along the midline. Physiologically, the left corpus cavernosum governs contributes to body rigidity and expansion. The crura of clitoris (Crura clitoridis) is two proximal cavernous limbs fixed to the inferior pubic and ischial rami. Physiologically, the crura of clitoris anchor the erectile body to pelvic bone.

Clinically, regarding the clitoral glans, do not describe the glans as a paired cavernous body. From a diagnostic standpoint, in the clitoral prepuce, its form and degree of coverage vary normally. In clinical pathology involving the clitoral body, the externally visible part understates total size. Medical evaluation of the right corpus cavernosum also notes that separate it anatomically from the vestibular bulb.

questions.question: Is the clitoris only the visible glans?
questions.answer: No. The visible glans is part of a larger erectile complex that includes a body, paired crura and associated vestibular bulbs. Structurally, the clitoral body (Corpus clitoridis) comprises midline body formed by apposition of the paired corpora cavernosa, deep to the external glans. Physiologically, the clitoral body governs engorges via cavernous vascular spaces.

questions.question: Where are the clitoral crura located?
questions.answer: The crura extend along the ischiopubic rami beneath the vulvar surface and join the midline erectile body. The crura of clitoris (Crura clitoridis) is two proximal cavernous limbs fixed to the inferior pubic and ischial rami. Physiologically, the crura of clitoris anchor the erectile body to pelvic bone.
